issues.text: The docs say a ClusterIP Service is "only reachable from within the cluster", which includes the nodes, not only Pods. Executed from kind node donhang-worker: `curl http://10.96.216.108:8080/health` returned HTTP 404 from the api, i.e. the node reached the cluster IP. "from Pods" reads as the only allowed origin.
issues.quote: Its address can be reached only from inside the cluster: from Pods, not from the browser on your laptop.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Its address can be reached only from inside the cluster, for example from a Pod, not from the browser on your laptop."

issues.text: `wget` is a tool name I have not met. The same sentence says what it does (fetches the page at an address), so I can follow, but I would stop for a second to wonder whether I need to know it.
issues.quote: fetches the page at the given address with `wget` and prints only its `<title>`
issues.fix: Drop the tool name: "fetches the page at the given address and prints only its `<title>`"; or add "(a command-line tool that sends a GET request)" after `wget`.

issues.text: Two script lines are never mentioned in the prose: the `kubectl wait --for=jsonpath=...` line and the `comm -13 <(...) <(...) | wc -l` line. The output tells me what they produce, so the main idea is safe, but I cannot tell what `wait` waits for or how 'new' addresses are counted.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after the helpers paragraph: "After the delete, the script waits until the Deployment has three Pods available again, then counts how many Pod addresses were not in the list from before."

issues.text: The output has an `EXTERNAL-IP` column showing `<none>`. The prose explains `TYPE` and the `...`, but not this column. It looks related to 'reachable only from inside the cluster', yet nothing confirms that, so I guess.
issues.fix: Add to the paragraph after the output: "`EXTERNAL-IP` is `<none>`: nothing outside the cluster can reach this Service." (only if that is accurate; otherwise say the column belongs to a later topic).

issues.text: I know 'endpoint' as an API endpoint (an HTTP method plus a path). Here `Endpoints` means Pod addresses. The step does say what the line lists, which saves me, but the clash with the meaning I learned is a stumble.
issues.quote: Note the `IP` line and the `Endpoints` line, which lists the addresses of the Pods behind the Service.
issues.fix: Add "(not the API endpoints of earlier lessons)" after "the `Endpoints` line".

issues.text: Expected result says each Endpoints address ends in `:80`, but the lesson never said the list holds address plus port. I can guess it is `targetPort`, but I am not sure whether it is `port` or `targetPort` (both 80 here).
issues.quote: while the `Endpoints` line shows different addresses, each ending in `:80`.

issues.text: The diagram names the Pods `web-a`, `web-b`, `web-c`, while the prerequisite taught that Pod names are the ReplicaSet name plus a random ending, and the output shows `web-...-...`. Small doubt whether these are real names.
issues.fix: Add to the first prose paragraph after the diagram: "(the Pod names are shortened)".

issues.text: q6 explanation for option c brings in 'one Pod cannot share the load'. The lesson says connections are spread across Pods, but never calls this sharing load or argues why one Pod is not enough. It adds an idea right where I am checking my reasoning.
issues.quote: But a bare Pod is not replaced when it is lost, and one Pod cannot share the load.
issues.fix: Replace "one Pod cannot share the load" with "connections cannot be spread across several Pods".
